problem: "Notice that only torsion gives shear stress; the other two give normal stress" contradicts Section 1, which gives direct shear τ = V/A. A shear force V is also an internal resultant and it does produce shear stress, so a student can take away the wrong rule that shear stress comes only from torque.
fix: "Of these three resultants, only torque gives shear stress; P and M give normal stress. A shear force V also gives shear stress, as τ = V/A."

problem: The same radial coordinate is written as r in τ = Tr/J and as ρ in J = ∫ ρ² dA, with no statement that they are the same quantity. A student may think they are two different distances.
fix: Use one symbol throughout, for example: "Let r be the radial distance from the axis in m; J = ∫ r² dA in m⁴."

problem: "gives stress in N/mm² = MPa only after correct conversion" does not say which way the error goes, so it cannot be used as a check.
fix: "M in N·m with y or r in mm and I or J in mm⁴ gives a number 1000 times smaller than the stress in MPa; convert M and T to N·mm first, then the result is directly in N/mm² = MPa."
